searchText: The WebAssembly working group wants to finalize SIMD instructions, I don't think we use much beyond SHA256 on 2/4 ints at once do we? https://github.com/WebAssembly/simd/issues/343 <@551157969367334912> if you shut the node down, you can extract the entire state (with or without code) as jsonl output. See 'geth dump -h'. It's better than rpc when working with huge data, since it doesn't amass 5Gb of data in the pipeline before sending (or trying to) over rpc <@!570268431522201601> , maybe 256-bitwise opcodes like XOR can be accelerated in SIMD. <@!211091239112671234> Interesting, I will try that as well, seems a straightforward solution. I'll also try to create a module for turbo-geth which could query directly what I need, as suggested by me through twitter. https://twitter.com/mandrigin/status/1312843393987379208?s=20 A friend also suggested me to use this https://github.com/blockchain-etl/ethereum-etl, which also seems a good solution.
